Founded in 1899, the club competes in [[Serie A]], the top tier of [[Italian football league system|Italian football]]. In its early history, Milan played its home games in different grounds around the city before moving to its current stadium, the [[San Siro]], in 1926.{{Cite news |date=2023-09-27 |title=AC Milan: Serie A club plan to move out of San Siro to new 70,000-capacity stadium |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66938991 |access-date=2024-05-28 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=29 May and has been shared with [[Inter Milan]] since 1947,{{cite web |title=History of San Siro stadium |url=https://www.sansirostadium.com/en/stadium/History |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813023024/https://www.sansirostadium.com/en/stadium/History |archive-date=13 August 2022 |access-date=8 July 2022}} is the largest in [[Football in Italy|Italian football]], with a total capacity of 75,817.{{cite web |title=San Siro Stadium – "La Scala del Calcio" |url=https://sansirostadium.com/the-stadium/?lang=en |website=San Siro Stadium |access-date=6 February 2026 |archive-date=30 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930203706/https://sansirostadium.com/the-stadium/?lang=en |url-status=live }} The club has a long-standing rivalry with Inter, with whom they contest the ''[[Derby della Madonnina]]'', one of the most followed derbies in football.{{cite web|url=https://lowerblock.com/articles/the-biggest-rivalries-in-world-football/|title=The Biggest Rivalries in World Football|access-date=12 May 2025|archive-date=12 May with the exception of the 1980–81 and 1982–83 seasons.{{cite web |title=History |url=http://www.acmilan.com/en/club/history |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101007130309/http://www.acmilan.com/en/club/history |archive-date=7 October 2010 |access-date=4 October 2010 |work=acmilan.com October 2010 |publisher=BBC}} [[Silvio Berlusconi]]’s 31-year tenure as Milan president was a standout period in the club's history, as they established themselves as one of Europe's most dominant and successful clubs. Milan won 29 trophies during his tenure, securing multiple [[Serie A]] and [[UEFA Champions League]] titles. During the [[1991–92 Serie A|1991–92 season]], the club notably achieved the feat of being the first team to win the [[Serie A]] title without losing a single game. Milan is home to multiple [[Ballon d'Or]] winners, and three of the club's players, [[Marco van Basten]], [[Ruud Gullit]], and [[Frank Rijkaard]], were ranked in the top three on the podium for the [[1988 Ballon d'Or]], an unprecedented achievement in the history of the prize.{{Cite web |last=Leiva |first=Juanma |date=2023-05-10 |title=AC Milan vs Inter: which Champions League semi-finalist is the bigger club? |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/ac-milan-vs-inter-which-champions-league-semi-finalist-is-the-bigger-club-n/ |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=AS USA |language=en-us |archive-date=7 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007095556/https://en.as.com/soccer/ac-milan-vs-inter-which-champions-league-semi-finalist-is-the-bigger-club-n/ |url-status=live }} Milan is one of the [[List of football clubs by competitive honours won|most successful football clubs in the world]] in terms of total trophies won. Domestically, Milan has won 19 [[List of Italian football champions#Clubs|league titles]],{{cite web |title=Albo d'oro |url=http://www.legaseriea.it/it/serie-a-tim/albo-d-oro |url-status=live Al Ahly is the most successful club in the world |publisher=Football Magazine |date=22 February 2014 |access-date=22 December 2014 |archive-date=22 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222220833/http://www.football-magazine.it/en/il-milan-perde-il-trono-lal-ahly-e-il-club-piu-titolato-al-mondo/ |url-status=live }} The club has won seven European Cup/[[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] titles, making them the competition's second-most successful team behind [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], and further honours include five [[UEFA Super Cup]]s, two [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]]s, a joint recordShared with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] two [[Latin Cup]]s, a joint recordShared with [[Boca Juniors]], [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]], [[Peñarol]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] three [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]]s and one [[FIFA Club World Cup]]. Milan is one of the wealthiest clubs in Italian and world football.{{cite news |title=Soccer Team Valuations |url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/2008/34/biz_soccer08_Soccer-Team-Valuations_Rank.html |work=forbes.com |date=30 April 2008 |access-date=4 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100929163532/http://www.forbes.com/lists/2008/34/biz_soccer08_Soccer-Team-Valuations_Rank.html |archive-date=29 September 2010| url-status= live}} It was a founding member of the now-defunct [[G-14]] group of Europe's leading football clubs as well as its replacement, the [[European Club Association]].{{cite web |title=ECA Members |url=http://www.ecaeurope.com/Default.aspx?id=1082680 |work=ecaeurope.com |publisher=[[European Club Association]] |access-date=4 October 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100604081402/http://www.ecaeurope.com/Default.aspx?id=1082680 |archive-date=4 June 2010}} [[File:San siro stadium.jpg|thumb|250px|right|An aerial view of the San Siro]]"}}
